title: Your Finance Agent's Bottleneck Is You — Ramana Siddanth Emani, Auditoria AI
talk_summary: A finance-agent practitioner argues the real bottleneck is the developer's own attention and dev-loop velocity, not model capability, and proposes four primitives: parallel sub-agents in isolated git worktrees, org-specific skills, MCP tool access, and a single-pane minimal UX. He then sketches removing the human from the loop via goals+loops, agents analyzing their own bottlenecks, and 'dreaming' over production sessions.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each task (e.g. a QA bug ticket) gets its own isolated git worktree and its own agent, which may spawn further sub-agents; tasks are not queued behind each other.
takeaways.evidence_quote: different work trees are handled by a separate agent, and these agents can spawn multiple sub-agents to solve that particular task. You don't want to queue up your tasks
takeaways.numbers: claims ~50 active worktrees/sub-agents on a 48GB MacBook

takeaways.what_they_do: Encode the organization's correct workflows as reusable skills handed to agents so they follow the proper procedure for each class of production bug rather than improvising.
takeaways.evidence_quote: These are your organization secret recipes. So, make sure you have a lot of skills because these skills, once you start say giving it to your agents, the agents will always make sure to use the correct and proper workflows

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one-shot prompts, set a persistent goal and let a loop iterate on it (e.g. 'fix this data discrepancy') so the agent keeps working without human re-prompting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what if you combine goals and loops? You can just set a goal saying there is some data discrepancy in this report

takeaways.technique: Agent analyzes its own harness bottlenecks
takeaways.what_they_do: After running the loop for a day or two on real tickets, ask the agent to list the bottlenecks in its own process and remove them incrementally each day.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just tell the agent to analyze all the bottlenecks in this process. Make a list of them. And somehow slowly keep removing these bottlenecks every day
takeaways.numbers: claims ~1 month to a one-sentence 'fix this bug' loop

takeaways.what_they_do: Background process ingests customer/production sessions, compacts recurring patterns and problems into data points the system can learn from.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you let the agent dream like humans dream in the background so that it collects all the sessions that your customers are using and compacts it into a set of data points

takeaways.what_they_do: Collapse dashboards, logs, tickets, PRs and agent sessions into one widget to cut the human's context-switching ('neck rotations') while supervising agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just compress all of this into one pane of glass because minimal UX is the key
